facts.title: The First Known Computer Algorithm Was Published With Literary Footnotes Longer Than the Paper Itself
facts.fact: In 1843, Ada Lovelace translated Luigi Menabrea's French article on Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine and appended seven 'Notes' labeled A through G. Her footnotes were nearly three times longer than the original engineering paper and contained Note G, the first published algorithm for computing Bernoulli numbers.
facts.context: Lovelace called her approach 'poetical science', blending mathematical logic with literary imagination. She also predicted that computing machines could one day compose music and manipulate symbols beyond pure arithmetic.

vocab.definition: The strange wistfulness and rich atmosphere of used bookstores, filled with thousands of old books you may never have time to read.
vocab.example: Walking into the quiet corner of the central library before semester exams gave everyone a sudden sense of vellichor.
vocab.etymology: Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, blending 'vellum' (parchment) and 'ichor' (ethereal fluid).
